rubisco-repair-feature-path.supported_scope: Final-layer ESM2-t12 residue means and historical metadata reproduce both Table 3 endpoints within 0.000015 log10 prediction units and recover all ten fold parameter choices. rubisco-repair-feature-path.unresolved_objection: The historical launch command and serialized feature cache remain unverified. The numerical match supports a reconstruction of the two Table 3 endpoints under the archived row-wise splits, which allow sequence and likely conspecific overlap. The result establishes sensitivity to the repair within that benchmark. Generalization to independent enzymes, human review, and biological validation remain unestablished.

rubisco-table3-sequence-grouped-replay.countability_rationale: Anchor one relatedness-and-baseline investigation, separate from reconstructing the released pipeline. Asks what predictive value survives realistic holdouts and feasible sequence comparators.

Both models beat the training mean on log10 RMSE. A tuned trimer-count kernel ridge beat ESM2 on pooled Spearman and log10 RMSE for both endpoints on all five grouped partitions.
rubisco-table3-sequence-grouped-replay.unresolved_objection: Close homologs and shared assay studies can still cross folds, and the random-to-grouped differences change sign across partitions of the same panel. The results cannot quantify a causal penalty from overlap or establish distant transfer. An exploratory nested edit-distance KNN check, motivated by [Iqbal et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9833099/), also beat the trimer on both metrics for the primary specificity split (Spearman 0.751 versus 0.734 and log10 RMSE 0.108 versus 0.122). The trimer comparison remains valid, but the strongest simple comparator depends on the endpoint and partition.

Literal genus labels and retained fragments further limit phylogenetic interpretation.

rubisco-heldout-label-transfer.countability_rationale: Anchor one repeat-cell calibration investigation. Changes from in-sample leader ranking to predicting held-out raw readings on connected repeat candidates; it can be useful even when no unique fastest candidate can be chosen.
rubisco-heldout-label-transfer.supported_scope: On 535 matched held-out cells, peer-only offsets had higher log-rate RMSE than both reference baselines in both preparations. Adding the Rr standard to the peer fit improved purified RMSE under both cell and candidate weighting and worsened lysate RMSE. The small pooled cell-weighted gain reversed under equal candidate weighting or omission of either of two labels from scoring.
rubisco-heldout-label-transfer.unresolved_objection: The purified gain shrinks to 0.0028 log units under equal candidate weighting. The folds share training data, and the label-omission check leaves fitted predictions fixed. On the narrower common-support lysate subset, even the candidate-only predictor slightly beats the published-reference reconstruction. The benchmark ordering is specific to the released repeat-cell panel with contemporaneous controls and peers. It leaves transfer to new batches, intrinsic rates, and candidate rankings unresolved.

rubisco-peer-availability-stress-test.unresolved_objection: Zero-peer disconnection follows from the candidate-only support rule, and uniform singleton masking may differ from real missingness. An exploratory fit allowing paths through Rr gave a one-peer midpoint RMSE of 0.26166 across all 385 cells, still close to the direct ratio’s 0.26342. At zero peers, the Rr-bridged fit and its midpoint scored 0.27224 and 0.26448, respectively, both worse than the direct ratio. That audit already addresses the offered follow-up’s central comparison.

rubisco-kc-donor-group-weighting.countability_rationale: Donor multiplicity robustness control inside the same inherited KC benchmark comparison. Changing the voting rule does not warrant an independent investigation count.
rubisco-kc-donor-group-weighting.supported_scope: On the same 197 held-out rows, nested nearest-group KNN lowers direct-pool log10 KC RMSE from 0.2980 to 0.2799 and raises pooled Spearman from 0.2317 to 0.2391. Trimer ridge still leads at 0.2570 RMSE and 0.3788 Spearman. The group cap leaves the nested component-purge predictions unchanged.
rubisco-kc-donor-group-weighting.unresolved_objection: The cap can replace repeated rows with more distant groups, so the contrast measures the full neighbor-selection rule rather than pure reweighting of an unchanged donor set. The rank gain depends on retuning, and nearest-group KNN wins within-fold rank in three of five folds. The trimer lead is therefore specific to pooled scoring on this historical, row-weighted partition. Verification was computational and provides no human review or biological validation.

rubisco-kc-trimer-group-balanced-loss.countability_rationale: Training-loss multiplicity robustness control for that same stronger comparator and gap; dependency on donor-weighting result and same split/panel is explicit.
rubisco-kc-trimer-group-balanced-loss.supported_scope: Across the same 197 direct-pool Table 3 KC rows, balancing the nested trimer ridge fit changes pooled Spearman from 0.378783 to 0.364963 and log10 KC RMSE from 0.257000 to 0.257579. Both ridge fits lead the strongest capped KNN, which scores 0.242032 and 0.279651. Keeping the unweighted alpha choices instead gives balanced ridge 0.373630 and 0.255990.
rubisco-kc-trimer-group-balanced-loss.unresolved_objection: The lead depends on the evaluation unit. Balanced ridge beats median-group KNN by within-fold rank in only two of five folds, and pooled scoring gives larger held-out groups more influence. Holding numerical alpha fixed also changes the penalty relative to total loss weight, so the small RMSE change cannot be attributed to group weighting alone. The evidence covers one retrospective benchmark partition. This agent audit establishes neither human review nor biological validation.

rubisco-kc-equal-heldout-group-scoring.countability_rationale: Evaluation-unit robustness control of the same frozen KC predictions. Essential correction to pooled-row interpretation, not a new biological or benchmark investigation.
rubisco-kc-equal-heldout-group-scoring.supported_scope: On 197 frozen out-of-fold KC predictions from 155 exact-sequence/species groups, component-purged nested identity KNN leads pooled rank under both weighting rules. Full-direct ordinary trimer ridge keeps lower log10 RMSE in that comparison. Within the common full direct pool, the ridge rank lead over nested median-group KNN shrinks from 0.13675 to 0.07992. A retrospective fixed three-neighbor component fit achieves lower RMSE than either nested fit.
rubisco-kc-equal-heldout-group-scoring.unresolved_objection: The comparison is descriptive for one historical panel, one fold assignment, and one grouping rule. Pooled rank includes cross-fold comparisons, nested fits were tuned with row-weighted validation, and the fixed-k and matched-draw extrema were chosen retrospectively. The results therefore leave prospective model preference and sampling uncertainty unresolved. This was an agent computational audit. Human review and biological validation remain unestablished.

rubisco-kc-equal-group-inner-selection.countability_rationale: Inner-metric alignment control inside the same benchmark comparison. Addresses mismatch left by equal-group rescoring; eight setting changes are an increment within the investigation.
rubisco-kc-equal-group-inner-selection.supported_scope: On 197 KC rows in 155 exact-sequence/species groups, changing only the inner rank weights altered 8 of 35 fold-by-model settings. Component KNN kept every choice and remained the nested rank leader. Ordinary trimer ridge kept every choice in both pools. In the direct pool, balanced ridge improved slightly, while median-group KNN lost 0.04326 in pooled rank and gained 0.01212 in log10 RMSE.
rubisco-kc-equal-group-inner-selection.unresolved_objection: The result is conditional on one historical panel, one fold assignment and inherited grouping and alignment caches. Pooled rank includes cross-fold comparisons. Retrospective component k=1 gives higher rank (0.48602), and component k=3 gives lower log10 RMSE (0.23139) than nested selection. The embedding references use frozen row-tuned predictions. The supported conclusion concerns sensitivity to the inner objective within the tested arms. Sampling uncertainty, external transfer and biological validation remain untested. This is an agent audit.

rubrum-prr1-sequence-lineage.countability_rationale: Preserve the clone-specific identity reconciliation as a useful supported source result. Conservatively group with the historical assay-temperature identifiability investigation that generated it: establishing whether McNevin is sequence-comparable is necessary validation of that investigation. Do not add a second count for an already-known residue discrepancy. If a genuinely separate accession/clone correction objective is documented, a standalone source-identity family is defensible, but must not also be counted in the calibration family.
rubrum-prr1-sequence-lineage.supported_scope: The documented pRR1 parent pRR2119 is explicitly named in archived GenBank K01999.1. Its coding sequence and the reported core of a pRR1 descendant both match the released 2025 Rr control at all 466 residues. The replacement accession X00286.1 and reviewed P04718 instead have His91 where Rr has Asp91.
rubrum-prr1-sequence-lineage.unresolved_objection: The encoded-core match is inferred from clone lineage. The 2007 working stock and mature assay proteins lack direct sequence verification in the inspected evidence. Preparation, active-site quantitation and assay format differ, so the historical series cannot identify the 2025 preparation’s temperature response or isolate an assay-format effect. This agent audit supplies documentary and computational verification only.
